info.title: 11 Estates CRM — web (edge BFF)
info.description:
Next.js app on Vercel (bom1). Responsibilities: Google sign-in (Supabase Auth), session and JWT validation, role
checks (coarse, per route), minting short-lived **service tokens**, routing (one hop), rate limiting (Postgres token
bucket), correlation IDs, users and roles (publishes `user.changed.v1` via its outbox), the immutable **audit log
sink**, and upload/export/user notifications (conventions R-6).
**No business rules** (ADR-0007): the owning service always re-checks role, tenant and resource permissions.

### Auth flow
1. Browser → `/auth/sign-in` (page) → Supabase Auth `signInWithOAuth({ provider: 'google' })` → Google consent.
2. Google → Supabase → `/auth/callback?code=…` (Next.js route handler) exchanges the code (PKCE) for a Supabase
   session. Session cookies: httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax. Sign-ups are disabled in Supabase; only invited emails
   exist.
3. web looks up `web.users` by the Supabase user id: missing or `deactivated` → sign out and `403 not-invited` /
   `user-deactivated`. First sign-in of an invited user flips status `invited → active`.
4. Every API call: Next.js middleware validates the Supabase access token (JWKS, `aud=authenticated`, `exp`), loads
   the user's role/tenant (cached 60 s in memory, invalidated on role change), enforces the 12 h idle timeout
   (`last_seen_at`), checks Origin on mutating requests (CSRF), takes a rate-limit token, then forwards.
5. Forwarding: web mints a **service token** (ES256 JWT, 5 min, `iss=web`, `aud=<service>`, `sub=web`, `tid`,
   `uid`, `role`, `dop` (data-operator flag), `jti`), cached per (user, audience) for 4 min, and sends
   `Authorization: Bearer <service token>`, `X-User-Id`, `X-User-Role`, `X-Tenant-Id`, `X-Correlation-Id`,
   `traceparent`, and the client's `Idempotency-Key` / `If-Match` unchanged. Client-supplied `X-User-*`/`X-Tenant-*`
   headers are stripped. Services verify signature (web JWKS), `aud`, `exp`, and that headers equal the claims.
6. Outbound call policy: 2 s timeout (chat stream: 15 s), 1 retry with jittered backoff (100–400 ms) on idempotent
   methods only, circuit breaker per downstream (50% errors over 20 calls → open 30 s).

### Rate limits (Postgres token bucket in the `web` schema; conventions §4)
| Bucket | Key | Rate | Burst |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api` | user | 20 req/s | 40 |
| `chat_msg` | user | 30 / min | 30 |
| `chat_stream` | user | 1 concurrent (lease, 20 s max) | — |
| `upload` | user | 5 / hour (POST /v1/uploads) | 5 |
| `public_page` | client IP | 60 / min (GET /p/{token}) | 60 |
429 responses carry `Retry-After` and `code: rate-limited`. Headers `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `X-RateLimit-Remaining`
on every proxied response. If the bucket store is unavailable, web falls back to a per-instance in-memory limiter
(fail-open with a lower local limit) and raises an alarm.
The website's Listings API (API key) is **not** routed through web; listings enforces its per-key limit itself.

### Correlation IDs
`X-Correlation-Id` is accepted if it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,64}$`, otherwise a UUIDv7 is generated. It is returned
on every response, forwarded on every hop, logged on every line and copied into events by the services.

get.summary: Signed-in user, role, tenant, permissions, session expiry and environment flags (drives the UI)
get.x-rate-limit: api bucket (20 req/s, burst 40 per user)

delete.summary: Sign out (revokes the Supabase refresh token, clears cookies, drops cached service tokens)

get.summary: The caller's upload, export and user notifications (web-owned, R-6); journeys owns /v1/notifications for work notifications

200.description: Page sorted by createdAt desc, id

post.summary: Mark notifications read (listed ids, or everything up to a time)
post.x-idempotency: Naturally idempotent (setting read_at twice is a no-op); Idempotency-Key also accepted

get.summary: The five staff roles and their permission codes (PRD §2.3), read-only
Users of the tenant (Settings → Users & roles). Non-admins get a directory view (id, name, role, status) for pickers.

200.description: Page sorted by displayName, id (Admin sees email and audit fields)

post.summary: Invite a Google account by email with a role (Supabase Auth invite; expires in 7 days)
post.x-rate-limit: api bucket; plus 20 invitations per hour per tenant
post.x-idempotency: Idempotency-Key accepted (24 h, per user+route); replay returns the original invitation. Re-inviting an email with a pending invitation → 409 email-already-invited.

isDataOperator.description: Adds the Data operator permission to an agent (A-15)

201.description: Invited (user row created with status invited)

delete.summary: Revoke a pending invitation (the user row is marked deactivated; the Supabase invite is deleted)

patch.summary: Change role, data-operator flag, display name, or deactivate / reactivate (JSON Merge Patch)
patch.description:
Deactivation revokes all Supabase sessions for the user, evicts cached role and service tokens, and blocks
new tokens immediately (tokens already minted expire within 5 min). The last active Admin cannot be demoted or
deactivated (409 last-admin). Users cannot change their own role.
patch.x-idempotency: PATCH (JSON Merge Patch) is idempotent by design; If-Match with the row version → 412 on mismatch

get.summary: Immutable audit log (US-35), newest first; filters on stored fields

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Exact action or a prefix ending in ".*" (e.g. "export.*")

200.description: Page sorted by occurredAt desc, id

get.summary: Public keys that verify web-minted service tokens (current + previous during rotation)

post.summary: Mint a service-to-service token (aud=<target>, sub=<caller>, tid, 5 min) for projection rebuilds and background jobs
post.description:
Callers authenticate with their per-service credential. Allowed (caller → audience) pairs are fixed in config:
listings→records, journeys→records, insight→records, records→intake, crm-engine→records, and every service→records
for the vocabulary fetch (conventions R-2). Anything else → 403 audience-not-allowed. Tokens are never minted for
user-facing request chains between services.
post.x-idempotency: Not idempotent by nature (each call mints a new jti) and has no side effects beyond an issuance counter; Idempotency-Key is not needed — callers cache the token for 4 min

post.summary: Publish unpublished outbox rows (user.changed.v1) to consumer queues (pg_cron every minute + poke after commit)
post.x-rate-limit: none (scheduler only; single-flight via advisory lock)
post.x-idempotency: Idempotent (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; published_at set in the same transaction as pgmq.send)

post.summary: Consume q_web: audit.recorded.v1 → audit_log; upload.completed.v1 / upload.failed.v1 / export.completed.v1 / export.failed.v1 → notifications
post.x-rate-limit: none (scheduler only; every minute + poke from producer relays)
post.x-idempotency: Idempotent (processed_events dedupe; audit_log unique on event_id)

post.description:
- `invitation-expire` (hourly): pending invitations older than 7 days → expired.
- `idle-session-sweep` (every 15 min): revoke Supabase sessions idle > 12 h (NFR-16).
- `notification-prune` (daily): delete notifications older than 90 days.
- `rate-limit-prune` / `idempotency-prune` (hourly).
- `audit-chain-verify` (daily): re-verify the audit hash chain for the last 48 h; alarm on a break.
- `signing-key-rotate` (every 90 days): publish a new service-token key in JWKS, keep the previous one for 1 h.
- `keep-alive` (pilot only, every 12 h): trivial query so the free Supabase project is not paused.

200.description: DB reachable, migrations current, signing key loaded, Supabase Auth JWKS cached; checks lists each downstream circuit state

staffSession.description: Supabase Auth access token for a signed-in, invited staff user (from the httpOnly session cookie via Next.js middleware, or an Authorization header).

serviceCredential.name: X-Service-Credential
serviceCredential.description: Per-service client secret (Vercel env of the caller; hashed in web.service_clients). Only for /internal/v1/service-tokens.

cronSecret.name: X-Cron-Secret
cronSecret.description: Per-service secret used by Supabase pg_cron/pg_net for /internal/v1/relay, /internal/v1/drain/*, /internal/v1/jobs/*.

permissions.description: Permission codes from PRD §2.3, e.g. publication.set, users.manage, audit.read

pilot.description: Phase 1a: shows the "sample/anonymised data only" banner (CR-005)

title.description: No PII, e.g. "UPL-000231 processed: 19,870 accepted, 130 rejected"

eventId.description: Source event (null for web's own entries)

action.description: e.g. contact.viewed, export.created, merge.done, merge.undone, publication.set, demand.exited, deal.closed, settings.changed, user.invited

actorDisplayName.description: Resolved from web.users at read time

entryHash.description: SHA-256 over the previous hash + this entry (tamper evidence)

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: UUID; 24 h replay window per user+route. Same key with a different body → 409 idempotency-key-reused.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: Row version for optimistic concurrency; mismatch → 412 version-mismatch.

x-routes.description:
Routing table (evaluated top-down, first match wins; `*` = one path segment, `**` = the rest). web adds auth headers
and forwards the request unchanged to `<service base URL><path>`. For proxied routes web checks only authentication,
active status and tenant; role rules live in the owning service (single source of truth, no drift). web applies
roles itself only to its own endpoints. Anything not listed → 404 route-not-found.

table.note: work notifications (R-6); web's upload/export/user notifications are /v1/me/notifications
proposal share page (token in path); rate limit public_page per IP
POST /v1/uploads also takes an upload bucket token (5/h)
SSE passthrough, no buffering; chat_msg + chat_stream buckets
never routed; services expose /internal only to pg_cron/pg_net (X-Cron-Secret) or to service tokens
